\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دلتنگ} \fa{شدن} (deltang shodan)}{دلتنگ شدن (deltang shodan)}]{\fa{دلتنگ} \fa{شدن} (deltang shodan) — to miss (someone)}

\label{lesson:FA-C257-deltang-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to travel, then the Persian for to retire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دلتنگ} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{دلتنگ} \fa{شدن}} — \emph{deltang shodan} — \textquotedblleft{}to miss (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{deltang shodan} is \textquotedblleft{}to become narrow-hearted\textquotedblright{}: \emph{del}, \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{} (inherited, EtymDB), with \emph{tang}, \textquotedblleft{}narrow\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{shodan}. All are native Persian. \emph{shodan}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{šudan}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بزرگ} \fa{شدن} (bozorg shodan)}{بزرگ شدن (bozorg shodan)}]{\fa{بزرگ} \fa{شدن} (bozorg shodan) — to grow up}

Before the new one: say the Persian for to retire, then the Persian for to miss.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بزرگ} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{بزرگ} \fa{شدن}} — \emph{bozorg shodan} — \textquotedblleft{}to grow up\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{bozorg shodan} is \textquotedblleft{}to become big\textquotedblright{}: \emph{bozorg} is inherited, from Middle Persian \emph{wuzurg} (EtymDB). \emph{shodan}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{šudan}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{احساس} \fa{کردن} (ehsâs kardan)}{احساس کردن (ehsâs kardan)}]{\fa{احساس} \fa{کردن} (ehsâs kardan) — to feel}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{احساس} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{احساس} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{ehsâs kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to feel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ehsâs kardan} pairs \emph{ehsâs}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{iḥsās}, \textquotedblleft{}perceiving, feeling\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{ḥ-s-s}, Lane), with the Persian verb \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do, to make\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\fa{قول} \fa{دادن}} — \emph{qol dâdan} — \textquotedblleft{}to promise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qol dâdan} pairs \emph{qol}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{qawl}, \textquotedblleft{}saying, word\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{q-w-l}, Lane), with the Persian verb \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}. \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*deh\textsubscript{3}-}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
